lesson.title: Containers from Zero, part 10: clean up, and the edge of one machine
lesson.shortTitle: Clean up, and the edge of one machine
lesson.description: Remove the notes app and everything the series created, with a last backup first, and check that Docker's disk usage is back to zero. Then see what Compose does on one machine, what it leaves to a cluster, and where Kubernetes from Zero picks up.
lesson.tested: Removed every object the series made, back to zero in docker system df, Engine 29.10.1, 25 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Project commands clean up a project; prune commands clean up the whole machine, so read their warning before you answer y.

boards.title: What each command removes

rows.name: down -v --rmi local
rows.role: Also named volumes, attached anonymous volumes, and images it built without a custom tag.

rows.name: image rm NAME
rows.role: Those images; refused while a container, even stopped, uses one.

rows.name: builder prune
rows.role: Build cache. Later builds recreate it.

rows.name: system prune
rows.role: Stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images, unused build cache; `--volumes` adds unused anonymous volumes.

rows.name: volume prune
rows.role: Unused anonymous volumes; `-a` unused named ones too.

boards.note: Every prune lists what it will remove and asks [y/N]; `-f` skips the question. Unused means not used by at least one container.

boards.title: The edge of one machine
boards.hint: Compose talks to one Docker Engine

rows.name: Where it runs
rows.role: One engine, local or remote through `DOCKER_HOST`.

rows.name: Machine stops
rows.role: The app stops with it; restart policies act when the engine starts again.
rows.where: The manager starts replacements on other machines.

boards.note: Docker's guide: the easiest deployment is a single server. Kubernetes from Zero teaches the cluster side.

steps.title: What the lab showed
steps.hint: sizes and IDs differ on your machine

items.what: `docker system df`: Images 10, 736.4MB; Containers 2; Local Volumes 1, 65.94MB; Build Cache 24, 76.52MB.
Backup of 98 lines, then `down -v --rmi local` removed containers, network, `notes_db-data` and `notes-web`.
`hello-web` via `down --rmi local`; the rest via `docker image rm`. `Untagged` removes a name, `Deleted` the image.
Every `docker system df` row 0 and 0B; only `bridge`, `host`, `none` networks left.

steps.note: Safety: deletes `notes_db-data` and the notes after saving `~/notes-backup.sql`, the series' images, unused build cache and the `hello` and `notes` folders. No port is published. There is no undo beyond the backup.

commands.cmd: docker compose exec db pg_dump -U notes notes > ~/notes-backup.sql
docker image rm hello-app:1.0 hello-app:1.1 hello-app:1.2 hello-app:latest

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What do `-v` and `--rmi local` add to `docker compose down`?
exercises.a: `-v` removes named volumes from the file and anonymous volumes attached to the containers. `--rmi local` removes images it built without a custom tag.

exercises.q: Why does `--rmi local` remove `notes-web` but not `postgres:18-alpine`?
exercises.a: Compose built and named `notes-web`; the file names `postgres:18-alpine`, a custom tag.

exercises.q: What does `docker volume prune` remove by default, and with `-a`?
exercises.a: Unused anonymous volumes; with `-a`, all unused volumes, named ones too.

exercises.q: Why does the lab remove objects by name instead of running `docker system prune -a --volumes`?
exercises.a: Prune covers the whole machine: it would also remove other work's stopped containers and unused images.

exercises.q: What does a cluster manager do when a machine with two replicas crashes?
exercises.a: It creates two new replicas on other machines, to match the desired state.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose ls -a` before step 2. Why is `hello` missing while `hello-web` is still an image?
exercises.a: Part 6 removed hello's containers, and the list is based on containers. `down` without `--rmi` left the image.

exercises.q: Run `docker image rm hello-app:1.1`. Why is there no `Deleted` line?
exercises.a: `hello-app:latest` still points at the same image ID; only the name was removed.

exercises.q: Run `docker system prune --volumes` and answer N. Name three things it would remove.
exercises.a: Any three of: stopped containers, unused networks, unused anonymous volumes, dangling images, unused build cache.

exercises.q: After the lab, run `docker network ls`. Which networks remain, and can you remove them?
exercises.a: `bridge`, `host`, `none`. No: `bridge is a pre-defined network and cannot be removed`.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A stopped `hello-world` container exists. What does `docker image rm hello-world` do?
exercises.a: It refuses: `conflict: unable to delete hello-world:latest (must be forced)`, naming the container. Remove the container first.

exercises.q: You run `docker compose down -v --rmi local` without the backup. Can you get the notes back?
exercises.a: No. The volume and the notes in it are deleted.

exercises.q: You run `docker compose down` in your home folder. What happens?
exercises.a: `no configuration file provided: not found`. Run it in the project folder.

exercises.q: The machine running the notes app shuts down. Does Compose start the app on another machine?
exercises.a: No. Compose works with one engine; the app stops with the machine. Moving work between machines is what a cluster manager does.
